study.title: Differential Influence of Acupuncture Somatosensory and Cognitive/Affective Components on Functional Brain Connectivity and Pain Reduction During Low Back Pain State
study.study_design: Randomized controlled trial; parallel-group fMRI study with two continuous pain runs (LBEpre and LBEpost) before and after acupuncture stimulation
study.randomization: Patients were randomized into either the REAL or PHNT group
study.blinding: Not explicitly described; patients in PHNT were told they would be stimulated with real acupuncture needles; needling credibility assessed retrospectively via in-depth interview
study.population: Patients with non-specific low back pain (LBP)
study.inclusion_criteria: Reported LBP of greater than four on a visual analog scale (VAS; 0 = no pain, 10 = most pain imaginable) when their low back was lifted (4–7 cm) in the supine position
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) LBP greater than four during baseline, (2) severe pain other than LBP (e.g., neck pain) at scan, (3) severe radicular pain extending into lower leg, (4) psychiatric or cardiovascular disorders, (5) accident- or surgery-related back pain, (6) back pain from metastatic cancer, vertebral fracture, spinal infection, inflammatory spondylitis etc., (7) taking medication for pain management (e.g., corticosteroid, narcotics, muscle relaxants, and any herbal medicine), (8) receiving acupuncture treatment for back or neck pain within a month, and (9) participating any previous acupuncture studies

arms.dropouts: 8 excluded: four due to incomplete scanning, three due to uncorrectable distortions, one due to excessive head motion (>2 mm)
5 excluded: four due to the absence of needling credibility, one due to excessive head motion (>2 mm)

conditions.scan_context: 6-min resting-state fMRI run; no pain stimulus applied; patients reported no pain during REST run

6-min continuous pain run using LBE pain model (individually calibrated air-cuff inflation under most painful area of low back); patients stayed still with eyes open staring at crosshairs; instructed to focus on perceived LBP intensity and sensations
conditions.dose_or_intensity_label: Individually calibrated air pressure targeting pain rating 4/10 VAS

conditions.scan_context: 7-min acupuncture stimulation run with real acupuncture needles; video recording of patient body projected in real time; acupuncturist stimulated needles in random order

7-min phantom acupuncture stimulation run; acupuncturist mimicked needling ritual without actual needles; previously recorded video from REAL group patient displayed on screen; no somatosensory needling afference
conditions.tissue_level_reasoning: Explicitly described as phantom acupuncture with no actual needles and no penetration. The acupuncturist only mimicked the needling ritual without any physical contact with needles, and a video of real acupuncture was displayed on screen as a visual illusion. No tissue engagement of any kind occurred.

conditions.scan_context: 6-min continuous pain run using LBE pain model; same air pressure intensity as LBEpre run applied
conditions.dose_or_intensity_label: Same individually calibrated air pressure as LBEpre

extraction_notes.note: Adverse events are not reported anywhere in the paper. The paper does not state whether adverse events were monitored or assessed.
The LBEpost pain scores (absolute values) are not explicitly reported for either group; only the change scores (LBEpost – LBEpre) are reported.

The abstract and results section report REAL pain change p-value as P < 0.005 and PHNT as P < 0.01, but the figure caption states 'P < 0.01 and 0.05, respectively' — there is a minor inconsistency between text and figure caption. The text values were used for extraction.

The paper states the abstract correlation for REAL mPFC–pINS as 'P < 0.05' but the results section states 'P < 0.01'. The results section value (P < 0.01) was used for the primary extraction as it is the more specific source.

No deqi/sensation scale scores with numerical values are reported for the current study. Sensation data are referenced from prior studies (Lee et al., 2014; Makary et al., 2018) rather than being collected as primary outcomes here.

No formal expectancy or blinding success questionnaire scores (e.g., Credibility/Expectancy Questionnaire) are reported. Credibility was assessed only via in-depth interview, and the specific content or scoring of the interview is not described.
Supplementary Figure S1 is referenced for ICA network maps and ROI locations but is not provided in the main PDF. Full network maps for DMN, SN, and SMN cannot be verified from the main document.

No whole-brain neuroimaging coordinate tables are reported. All neuroimaging results are based on ROI-level seed connectivity analyses. Coordinates are listed in Table 1 as ROI locations, not as peak activation coordinates from a contrast.

The paper does not report whether the dual-regression ICA and ROI connectivity analyses were corrected for multiple comparisons. The significance threshold is stated as P < 0.05 but no correction method is specified.

The S1back ROI coordinate is listed as MNI X = ±18, Y = −38, Z = 72 (bilateral). This represents two hemispheres combined but is treated as a single ROI in analysis. The bilateral averaging approach is described but not further detailed.

The paper notes that randomization was not performed accurately or systematically, resulting in unbalanced allocation (REAL n=33, PHNT n=23) and significantly different baseline (LBEpre) pain scores between groups (P = 0.01). This limits direct between-group comparison of pain outcomes.
The paper does not report absolute post-treatment LBEpain values; only change scores and their statistical significance are provided.

Figure 4A shows functional connectivity brain maps with directional changes (mPFC–pINS in REAL; PCC–aINS and S1back–pINS in PHNT; increased dACC–MCC and aINS–pINS in PHNT). No coordinate table or numerical cluster statistics accompany the figure. Specific increase/decrease values for dACC–MCC and aINS–pINS in PHNT are not reported in the text.
The paper does not report individual deqi subscale scores (Mass Index components) for the current study sample. These are referenced from Lee et al., 2014 only.

The paper states the flip angle for functional imaging as 90° and for structural as 8°, and FOV as 230 × 230 mm (functional) and 256 × 256 mm (structural). These values appear internally consistent but are noted here for completeness.

No REST run functional connectivity results are reported as primary outcomes. The REST run data was used only to define ROIs (based on group map of REST run) to ensure independence from pain model and acupuncture stimulation.
The paper does not clarify whether the 34 interleaved axial slices fully covered all ROI locations (especially the superior S1back at Z = 72 mm). This is noted as a potential coverage concern.
